newsitem.title: TURKEY: Turkish bond yields rise slightly on politics.
newsitem.headline: Turkish bond yields rise slightly on politics.

text.p: Turkish bond yields firmed slightly around 0.50-0.70 points on Tuesday in thin trade on concerns over increased political tension as the opposition parties step up searches for a new government, bankers said.
Bond yields rose to 97.50-97.92 percent in the most heavily traded papers, but bankers said the central bank's funding through overnight repos was keeping rates relatively lower.
A persistent cash shortage because of hefty corporate tax payments due end-April also dominated the markets.
The central bank also keeps its control on the market amid worries over the fate of government. The bank intervened on Monday for the third day in a row to support the Turkish lira.
The lira opened at 135,300 per dollar, slightly weaker from 135,200 Monday close.
Overnight money rates are running at 71.75 percent level due to continuing cash squeeze. Overnight repo rates are at around 74-75 percent levels after Monday's 74.59 percent average.
Bulent Ecevit, leader of Democratic Left Party, will hold talks with other opposition leaders on forming a government excluding the Islamist Welfare Party of Prime Minister Necmettin Erbakan.

Deputy Prime Minister Tansu Ciller said the government would continue. Two ministers from her True Path Party (DYP) party had resigned last week and launched a campaign to pull the DYP out of the coalition government.
